Engineering highlights

The bugs I hunt and the systems I harden

The work I'm proudest of isn't a feature list — it's the failures that no longer happen in production.

01

Fixed a race condition in the mysql2 connection pool

Kitchen orders were crossing between invoices: session variables set for one bill were being read on a different pooled connection. I traced it to the pool handing connections between requests, and built an ejecutarSp helper that pins one connection per stored-procedure call — then rolled it out across the entire API.

02

Stopped partial commits inside stored procedures

Error logging inside several procedures was issuing a COMMIT before the ROLLBACK, leaving half-written sales in the database. I fixed the transaction handling — EXIT HANDLER, error log, then rollback — so a failed operation now leaves no trace.

03

Hardware bridges for a web-based POS

A browser POS still has to print receipts and read fingerprints. I built SFAC_PrintBridge — a cloud print bridge per branch over Socket.IO — and SFAC_HuellaBridge, a native bridge to a ZKTeco ZK9500 fingerprint reader via FFI (koffi), used to authorize admin actions with a full audit trail.

04

Production CI/CD and disciplined database migrations

GitHub Actions pipelines ship to Lightsail containers with per-environment secrets (dev / prod), backed by versioned production migration scripts — plus cleanup and reset scripts that make each new POS rollout repeatable instead of improvised.

05

1,000 agents at 135–150 FPS, guarded by 103 tests

In the Unity game, a 1,000-sheep herd simulation runs above 130 FPS using GPU instancing — and stays correct because 103 Unity Test Framework tests cover the simulation, economy and save systems.
